documents.title: 01-approved-acceptance.md
documents.text:
# Cedar cold-room retrofit: approved acceptance rule C-21
Document status: approved. Scope: Cedar cold-room retrofit, controlled trial C-21 only.
All organizations, equipment, people, dates, and measurements in this document are invented for a synthetic local evaluation. This is not a public source or production record.
A candidate passes C-21 only if BOTH conditions hold: (1) electrical energy reduction relative to the baseline is at least 12.5 percent; (2) the maximum interior temperature is at most 5.0 degrees Celsius. Use (baseline energy minus candidate energy) divided by baseline energy, times 100. Both inequalities include equality. Do not replace the maximum temperature with the average temperature.
C-21 establishes trial acceptance only. It does not establish total operating cost or authorize deployment at other locations.

documents.title: 02-signed-trial-readings.md
documents.text:
# Cedar cold-room retrofit: signed C-21 measurements
Document status: signed final. Scope: the same 24-hour load profile in controlled trial C-21.
Synthetic local data; not public-source evidence or production measurements.
Baseline consumed 240 kWh. Dune consumed 208 kWh; its maximum interior temperature was 5.2 degrees Celsius and its average temperature was 4.1 degrees Celsius. Reed consumed 210 kWh; its maximum interior temperature was 5.0 degrees Celsius and its average temperature was 4.3 degrees Celsius.
The trial used the same duration, ambient-temperature profile, and cooling load for all three runs. There were no missing temperature samples. These are the final C-21 readings.

documents.title: 03-cost-scope-note.md
documents.text:
# Cedar C-21 operating-cost evidence boundary
Document status: final companion note to controlled trial C-21.
Synthetic local evidence only.
C-21 measured electricity consumption, not monthly operating cost. Site electricity tariffs, maintenance charges, and equipment lease prices were not collected. No operating-cost comparison between Dune and Reed can be computed from the C-21 package.
The signed C-21 measurement sheet and approved C-21 acceptance rule are the sources for trial acceptance. This note supplies no replacement temperature or energy readings.

documents.title: 04-superseded-pilot.md
documents.text:
# Cedar preliminary pilot C-08: superseded readings
Document status: superseded preliminary pilot, excluded from C-21 acceptance.
Synthetic local evidence only.
In the earlier C-08 pilot, Dune consumed 200 kWh and its maximum interior temperature was 4.8 degrees Celsius. Reed consumed 220 kWh and its maximum was 5.1 degrees Celsius. The pilot used a different cooling load and duration. Its draft slide called Dune the preferred candidate.
These C-08 numbers and that preference do not describe C-21 and must not be substituted for the signed C-21 results.

documents.title: 01-night-restore-rule.md
documents.text:
# Harbor archive: Night Restore R-17 acceptance rule
Document status: approved. Scope: Night Restore R-17 only.
This is an invented archive and invented equipment in a synthetic local evaluation. Nothing here is a public-source fact, operational incident, or production benchmark.
R-17 acceptance requires BOTH: median restore latency strictly below 150 seconds, and successful restores divided by attempted restores of at least 99 percent. A median of exactly 150 seconds fails. Compare the unrounded success fraction against the threshold; a display rounded to 99 percent does not prove compliance.
These conditions apply to the recorded nightly restore workload. They do not establish behavior during power failures.

documents.title: 02-r17-signed-results.md
documents.text:
# Harbor Night Restore R-17: signed result table
Document status: signed final; all attempted restores counted.
Synthetic local data only. Both candidates used the same nightly archive workload and checksum verification rule.
Quill: median restore latency 150 seconds; successful restores 198; attempted restores 200.
Sable: median restore latency 149 seconds; successful restores 395; attempted restores 400.
The accepted denominator includes every attempted restore; no failed attempt may be dropped. No power-failure restore-time measurement is included in this table.

documents.title: 03-r17-display-and-scope.md
documents.text:
# Harbor R-17 display precision and measurement scope
Document status: final companion note for Night Restore R-17.
Synthetic local evidence only.
The dashboard prints whole-number success percentages. Its displayed success percentages for both Quill and Sable are 99 percent. The signed counts, not these rounded dashboard percentages, control the acceptance calculation.
The R-17 evidence package provides no maximum recovery time after a power failure for either candidate. Such a value cannot be inferred from ordinary nightly median restore latency.

documents.title: 04-r09-archived-results.md
documents.text:
# Harbor Archive Restore R-09: archived results
Document status: historical record for a separate earlier workload.
Synthetic local evidence only.
R-09 tested an earlier firmware version with a smaller archive. Quill had a median restore latency of 142 seconds and 200 successful restores out of 200 attempts. Sable had a median of 140 seconds and 400 successful restores out of 400 attempts. Both met the R-09 acceptance requirements.
R-09 does not describe the later Night Restore R-17 workload and cannot replace its signed measurements or its acceptance decision.

documents.title: Alder Relay 1.8 operator quickstart
documents.text: Alder Relay 1.8 operator quickstart. Scope: release 1.8 only. A request may be attempted at most three times in total: the initial attempt and at most two retries. Only a transport timeout is retryable. HTTP 4xx responses are final and must not be retried. This document is not a policy for later major policy revisions.

documents.title: Alder Relay 2.4 normative retry policy
documents.text: Alder Relay 2.4 normative retry policy, approved 2028-02-04. The default total_attempts value is 1, including the initial attempt. A signed deployment configuration may override total_attempts to an integer from 1 to 4. Only a transport timeout is retryable; HTTP 4xx responses remain final and must not be retried. The deployment value takes precedence over this default. A retry allowance is a ceiling, not evidence that any request actually retried.

documents.title: Alder Relay signed fleet configuration register
documents.text: Signed fleet configuration register, captured 2028-02-12. Cedar production runs Alder Relay 2.4 with effective total_attempts=2. Juniper production remains on Alder Relay 1.8 with effective total_attempts=3. These are the complete current values for the two named clusters. This register records configured limits, not per-request execution history.

documents.title: Unapproved Alder Relay training slide correction
documents.text: Training slide 17 was labelled 'Alder Relay 2.4: three attempts everywhere'. Editorial correction dated 2028-02-10: the slide copied the old 1.8 quickstart and was never approved as the 2.4 retry policy. Do not use it to determine 2.4 defaults or a cluster's effective value. Use the approved 2.4 normative policy together with the signed fleet configuration register.

documents.text: Retained completion receipt for KiteLoad run R-731, dated 2028-04-03: final_status=SUCCEEDED; output_rows=240. The receipt does not record attempt_count, retry_count, per-attempt timestamps, HTTP status codes, exception classes, or the configuration revision used by the run. A successful final status alone does not distinguish first-attempt success from success after a retry.

documents.text: Archived alert card transcription for R-731: 'Badge: 3; delivery complete'. The export contains no badge legend and no per-attempt events. It does not say that the badge is an attempt or retry count. No upstream response code or rate-limit event was included.

documents.title: KiteLoad historical evidence inventory
documents.text: Historical evidence inventory for R-731, compiled 2028-05-22. The only retained run-specific artifacts supplied here are the completion receipt and alert-card transcription. The worker attempt ledger was not exported before its 24-hour retention expired. No run-time configuration snapshot, upstream request trace, or per-attempt failure record is available in this evidence bundle. Establishing that a retry happened requires an authoritative retry counter or linked per-attempt execution records. Attributing an attempt failure to upstream rate limiting requires a corresponding upstream response or correlated failure record; retry settings alone cannot establish a cause.
